transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, the exhibition opens to the public this Saturday, and before I give final approval on the public-opening package, I want to walk through the venue's proposed plan together. They've put forward an open-gallery display, visitor photography, standard gallery lighting, a 90-person hourly capacity, and three floor attendants. I'd like to hear from each of you — registrar, conservator, accessibility coordinator, and security manager — on any concerns or conditions you have before I make my decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. I reviewed the executed loan agreement this morning, and it contains several terms that directly conflict with the venue's proposed plan. Every borrowed costume must be displayed in a locked vitrine — not an open-gallery display. Visitor photography is prohibited. And the lender credit must read exactly 'Costumes courtesy of the Meridian Film Archive.' I haven't entered these terms in the opening checklist yet, but they are binding conditions from the lender.

transcript.text: I need to raise a serious conservation concern. My inspection found that the most fragile costume in the exhibition requires gallery humidity maintained between 45% and 55% and illumination no higher than 80 lux. I recorded the readings after yesterday's lighting test, but I haven't yet sent the report to Maya. Given that the venue has proposed standard gallery lighting, I need to flag that this may exceed what the most fragile costume can safely tolerate. We need to confirm the lighting levels will be at or below 80 lux before approval, and ensure the humidity controls are in place within that 45-55% range.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise an accessibility condition before approval. I completed my accessibility walkthrough with the venue this afternoon, and it confirmed two requirements that haven't been reflected on the floor plan yet. First, the public route through the exhibition must maintain at least 1.2 meters of clear width at all points. Second, three seats must be placed along the route for visitors who cannot stand through the full viewing sequence. I haven't updated the floor plan yet to show these, so I want to flag both as conditions that need to be confirmed before the package is approved.

transcript.text: I need to raise a security condition that must be reflected in the opening package before approval. I confirmed with the exhibition insurer today that admission must be capped at exactly 80 visitors per hour — not the 90 the venue has proposed — and that two credentialed guards must be present whenever the borrowed costumes are accessible to visitors. The insurer sent these conditions in today's coverage email, which I have not yet attached to the opening packet. These are binding insurance requirements, so the capacity and guard staffing both need to be updated accordingly before we proceed.
